content.title: China cements global lead in smart vacuums as Picea acquires Roomba maker iRobot
content.summary: Chinese robotics manufacturers are set to cement their dominance in the global smart vacuum market with Picea Robotics' acquisition of Roomba maker iRobot, after the US firm's proposed sale to Amazon.com last year fell through due to regulatory hurdles. China-based suppliers held the top five spots for worldwide smart robotic vacuum shipments in the first three quarters of 2025, led by Roborock with a 21.7 per cent market share, equal to 3.8 million units, according to data from research firm ID

content.title: iRobot Co-Founder Calls Silence on China Sale "Bizarre"
content.description: Helen Greiner, co-founder of iRobot, says she is "heartbroken" over the company's bankruptcy and the transfer of its assets to a Chinese supplier. In an interview on Bloomberg's Insight with Haslinda Amin, she told Paul Allen it's "bizarre" that there is no outcry over U.S. know-how moving to China. Greiner also warned that low-cost manufacturing will remain a challenge for the U.S., even with tariffs, due to a persistent shortage of skilled labor.
